title: The Cashman Wins Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Worth It?
description: The Cashman Wins review, checked 7 Nov 2026: $10 a month to $179 lifetime, no refunds, a seller kept pick sheet, and 33 CapperTek reviews read in full.
dek: Alan Cashman sells all access picks for $10 a month, $99 a year or $179 for life, far below most sellers. He posts a pick history sheet that he keeps himself. Buyers on CapperTek mostly praise him, but one reviewer wrote almost half the reviews, and two say they paid and got nothing.

short_answer: The Cashman Wins is a small, real service run by one named person, Alan Cashman, who says he is based in Indianapolis and appears on The Dan Dakich Show and WISH-TV. It publishes its prices, takes payment by card, Venmo, Cash App or X Money, and links a public pick history sheet. Most buyers who reviewed it on CapperTek say they got what they paid for.

Whether the picks make money is harder to say. The pick history is a Google Sheet that Cashman keeps himself, with odds and results but no time each pick was sent, so a buyer cannot confirm the picks were posted before the games. Win rates such as 65% to 70% come from the seller and from reviewers, not from an outside grader.
Because the price is so low, the money at risk is mostly what you bet, not the fee. If you join, record each pick with the time and line you received it, and compare that with the sheet.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on TheCashmanWins.com on 7 Nov 2026. The subscribe page lists the main plans. A separate "Previous Members" page showed lower prices, and the seller has posted many short term deals on TheRX forum.

guarantee: There is no guarantee. Every page on the site carries one line: "There are no refunds once picks are sent." The Terms and Conditions page we opened showed no other refund terms. The About page says plainly that he will not promise every play will win.

What that means in practice: at $10 a month the fee is small, but if picks do not arrive, as two CapperTek reviewers say happened to them, the written policy offers nothing. Both times the seller replied publicly that the buyer had access or that he would fix it.

claims_note: The "regular" prices move. On TheRX in February and March 2023 the Lifetime Pass was offered against a "Reg $399" price; by May and June 2023 the posts said "Reg $199"; on 7 Nov 2026 the subscribe page sold it for $179 and the Previous Members page listed $95 against "Reg $179". A discount measured from a regular price that keeps changing is a sales device, though every price we saw is low.

The dollar total on the pick sheet is built from stakes that change from pick to pick, from about $100 up to $2,500 in the rows we read, so it is not the same as a flat bet record. The short runs, such as 7-2 in a postseason, say little on their own.
record: What is the seller's own marketing, but more open than most: the Pick History page links a public Google Sheet with about 1,250 graded picks, mostly from 2019 to September 2026. Each row lists the league, date, game, pick, odds, result, units and dollars. That lets a buyer see losses as well as wins. But the sheet is kept by the seller, has no column for the time a pick was sent, and could be edited after the fact, so it is not independent proof. The newest row we saw was dated 27 Sep 2026.

What is independently verifiable: nothing we found. CapperTek, where most reviews appear, is a review directory, not a grader of this service's picks, and we found no third party leaderboard tracking Cashman. We found no court or regulator action involving Alan Cashman or TheCashmanWins.com in our searches.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition The Cashman Wins is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: reviewers and the seller cite 65% to 70% stretches. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: CapperTek showed 33 reviews from October 2022 to June 2026, and we read all of them. They come from 16 reviewer names, and one reviewer wrote 15 of the 33. Five reviews were posted between 31 Oct and 2 Nov 2022, and the seller has promoted the page on TheRX as "REAL Customer Reviews." Treat the sample as a small, loyal group rather than a broad survey. Below is each independent voice we found.

customers.text: One CapperTek reviewer posted 15 of the 33 reviews. He said he had been a member for more than five years, praised the price and honesty, and wrote that Cashman charges for a year what many sellers charge for a week. Most of his posts are short notes after good runs, and the seller replies to him by first name.

A reviewer said he paid $59 for two years of service, got nothing, and his emails went unanswered. The seller replied that he had answered every email, that the account had been active since 2 March, and that his messages were probably landing in spam.

A reviewer said he bought through Patreon and did not get a single pick. The seller replied that he had sent several emails, had heard of no problem, and offered to fix it if he had the wrong address.

A reviewer gave the service a thumbs up and called the price unbeatable, but said he was disappointed by how few plays are posted, with several days at a time without one, and found the computer models hard to choose from because they run hot and cold.

A reviewer who bought a lifetime pass wrote that every subscriber pick was documented on the site, that members also get spreadsheets of leans and his personal bets, and that Cashman usually answered email within the hour.

A reviewer said he had used the service for three years after hearing Cashman on The Dan Dakich Show, liked that he does not force daily picks, and had upgraded to a lifetime membership. In a later review he said he had won about 15 straight baseball picks.

Another reviewer said he had been a member for about two, then four, years, that he had winning football seasons every year, and that Cashman was honest and easy to contact. These are his claims; he posted no results.
A reviewer claimed Cashman is regularly over 65% every month on subscriber picks and averages about 15 to 20 picks a month. That win rate is the reviewer's statement, not a checked figure.

TheRX threads about the service are written by Cashman himself and contain only his own posts. Trustpilot had no page for thecashmanwins.com, SmartCustomer (formerly SiteJabber) showed 0 reviews, a Better Business Bureau search returned no matching business, and we found no Reddit discussion.

conflicts: The site has a Sportsbook Offers page and a menu link to "Join BetUS Sportsbook." The offers page uses referral or affiliate links for DraftKings, Caesars, BetMGM, BetUS and BetDSI, and the DraftKings link carries his name as the referrer. Referral and affiliate deals pay the referrer when readers sign up or deposit. BetUS and BetDSI are offshore sportsbooks that are not licensed by U.S. state regulators, so check the law where you live.
The BetUS page offers free picks through the Super Bowl for depositing $100 or more through his link, which ties the pick service directly to a sportsbook deposit.
strengths: Very low prices: $10 a month or $99 a year, so the fee is a small part of the risk.
A public pick history sheet with odds and results, losses included.
A named person who answers complaints in public, and most CapperTek reviewers report a good experience.
The About page says he will not promise winners and does not force daily plays.
concerns: The pick history is kept by the seller with no post times, so it cannot prove picks were sent before games.
No refunds once picks are sent, and two reviewers say they paid and received nothing.
The review sample is small and concentrated: one reviewer wrote 15 of 33 reviews.
Sportsbook referral links, including offshore books, and a free picks offer tied to a BetUS deposit.
"Regular" prices used for discounts have changed several times.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real, small service run by Alan Cashman, with published prices, a public pick sheet and mostly positive CapperTek reviews, though two buyers said they paid and got nothing. We could not verify that the picks win over time.
How much does The Cashman Wins cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 it cost $10 a month, $99 for a year with a second year free, or $179 for a lifetime pass, with lower prices of $45 to $95 on a Previous Members page. There are no refunds once picks are sent.
Does The Cashman Wins have a verified record?
No. The pick history is a Google Sheet kept by the seller, with odds and results but no post times, and no outside grader or Watchdog record tracks it.
Is The Cashman Wins worth it?

For a few dollars a week you get a small number of researched picks, computer model numbers and his personal bets, which several reviewers valued. What is unproven is whether the picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of bets, since the only record is the seller's own sheet.
